# dsh-opencli
Low-latency browser tools for DSH that drive the **local OpenCLI daemon directly** instead of spawni
ng the `opencli` CLI once per command.
`opencli` pays a Node cold start on every call — it resolves 318 modules to send one request (~1.4–1
.8 s per command; measured: `opencli list search` = 1071 ms). The daemon, once warm, answers the sam
e request in **5–20 ms**. This plugin keeps that daemon as a resident service: it posts to `http://1
27.0.0.1:19825/command` with the `X-OpenCLI: 1` header and hands the result straight back to the age
0.0.1:19825/command` with the `X-OpenCLI: 1` header and hands the result straight back to the agent.

-opencli version` for the current release).
**A · Inside DSH** — let the plugin manager resolve it from the registry:

From a checkout instead: `plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/dsh-opencli`
rom a checkout instead: `plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/dsh-opencli`.
**B · With the `dsh` CLI** — the CLI's `plugin` command forwards the rest of the line to pnpm inside
that profile directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**C · Manually, with npm / pnpm** — a DSH profile is an ordinary package directory, so the plugin is
an ordinary dependency:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Profiles created by the desktop app carry a pnpm `.npmrc` (`node-linker=hoisted`), so prefer `pnpm a
dd` there; plain `npm install dsh-opencli` also works in a profile that has no pnpm setup. Behind a
mirror: append `--registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`.
⚠️ **B and C only install the package** — neither touches `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the harness will
not load it until you enable the bundle (the sidebar's **Plugins** page, which both installs and se
lects; or the `plugin_manager` tool when your preset enables it). Route A does that step for you. Al
so keep the pnpm doing the install in step with the profile's lockfile: a v9 lockfile needs pnpm 10+
, and an older pnpm prints `Ignoring broken lockfile ... not compatible with current pnpm` and re-re
solves the whole profile (the desktop app ships its own pnpm 11.8 for exactly this reason).

very route finishes the same way: restart the session, or toggle the plugin entry `include:dsh-openc

## Tools
| Tool | What it does | Writes |
| `oc_status` | Daemon version, online state, extension connection, contextId, profiles, memory. The

first call when something breaks. | no |
| `oc_exec` | Runs JS expressions in your already-logged-i
n browser. `codes` runs up to 40 expressions in one round trip; evaluation is async, so `await fetch

(...)` works. | depends |
| `oc_navigate` | Opens a URL, waits for load, returns title / final URL /

whether it timed out. | yes |
| `oc_snapshot` | Compresses the page into a compact interactive stru
cture (title, links with href, buttons, inputs with name/placeholder, disabled flags) — an order of

magnitude cheaper than `outerHTML`. | no |
| `oc_tabs` | `list` / `new` / `select` / `close` tabs in

side the automation container. | new/select/close |
| `oc_screenshot` | Captures the viewport (or fu

ll page) to a PNG/JPEG file under the system temp dir and returns its path. | no |
| `oc_cookies` |

Reads cookies for one domain/URL scope — the logged-in session of the real browser. | no |
| `oc_net
work` | `start` / `read` a network capture buffer: URL, method, request headers, response status, bo

dy preview. | start/read |
| `oc_upload` | Attaches local files to a file input (CSS selector). | ye

s |
| `oc_input` | Inserts text into the focused element (typing into a real field). | yes |
| `oc_f

rames` | Lists the frames (iframes) of the current page. | no |
| `oc_cdp` | Calls one whitelisted C

hrome DevTools Protocol method (e.g. `DOM.getBoxModel`). | depends |
| `oc_chrome` | `describe` / `c

all` native Chrome management methods (tabs, tabGroups, windows). | call writes |
| `oc_close` | Clo

ses the automation window (`window`) or an owned tab (`tab`). | yes |
| `oc_download` | Waits for a
download matching a URL pattern and returns where it landed. | no |
`session` is the key of a persistent automation tab (default `dsh`), so different jobs get isolated
tabs for free. Every `oc_tabs` op takes a session (falls back to the configured default).
### Coverage
The tool set mirrors what the OpenCLI **daemon** can do, because that is the fast path (5–20 ms) and
the CLI's own sub-commands are only reachable by paying its 1.4–1.8 s cold start:
- Covered here: expression evaluation, navigation, tab management, snapshots, screenshots, cookies,
network capture, file upload, text input, frames, whitelisted CDP calls, native Chrome tab/group/win

dow management, window/tab closing, and download waiting.
- Not covered here: the OpenCLI **site ada
pters** (176 of them — GitHub, Xiaohongshu, Twitter, …) and the CLI-only browser verbs (`click`, `fi
ll`, `scroll`, `dialog`, …). Those run inside the `opencli` CLI process, not behind the daemon, so w
rapping them here would reintroduce the cold start this plugin exists to avoid. Drive them with the
`opencli` CLI directly, or use `oc_exec` / `oc_cdp` against the same page.
`oc_cdp` is restricted to a whitelist of CDP methods (`DOM.*`, `Page.captureScreenshot`, `Input.disp
atchMouseEvent`, `Runtime.enable`, …); `Runtime.evaluate` is denied by the extension, so use `oc_exe
Runtime.enable`, …); `Runtime.evaluate` is denied by the extension, so use `oc_exec` for JavaScript.
`oc_chrome` operates the browser's **native** tabs, groups and windows — not the automation containe
r. Native tabs survive after the session ends, so treat `oc_chrome op=call` as a user-visible write.
